checks.claim: Escalators are built at a slope of no more than 30 degrees, and 30 degrees is the standard.
checks.why: Sources give 30 degrees as the standard angle and the code maximum.

sources.title: Elevating experiences: escalators in public spaces (USC Illumin)

checks.claim: An escalator's steps ride on two sets of wheels running in two tracks, which keep each step level.
Safety codes require escalators to have a brake that stops them when the power fails.
checks.why: Pennsylvania and California codes require a brake that stops the escalator when the circuit opens.
